key_insight: Combining a spatially aware hybrid graph neural network with contrastive pretraining yields more accurate and robust power-outage predictions under extreme weather by capturing both grid topology and geographic proximity while improving representation quality from limited labeled events.
problem_solved: Predicting weather-driven power outages is hard due to sparse labels, heterogeneous spatial relationships (topology vs geographic adjacency), and noisy multi-source data; this paper addresses those challenges to improve early outage detection and prioritization.
method: Hybrid spatial GNN that fuses electrical-grid topology and geographic adjacency to model both network connectivity and spatial influence.
Contrastive learning pretraining on multi-source inputs (weather, asset/location features, historical outages) to learn robust node/region representations with limited labels.
Fine-tuning downstream outage prediction with disturbance-aware loss and spatio-temporal features for improved detection and localization.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building label-efficient, spatially informed ML models for critical infrastructure — improving generalization and early-warning capability in operational power systems and other spatial networked domains.
visual_elements: Map-based heatmap showing predicted vs actual outage regions over time (spatio-temporal animation frames).
Architecture diagram illustrating hybrid GNN layers (topology + geographic edges) feeding into contrastive pretraining and downstream classifier.
Bar/line chart comparing performance metrics (AUC/Recall/F1) against baselines with and without contrastive pretraining.
Data-flow infographic showing multi-source inputs (weather forecasts, grid topology, asset attributes, historical outages) into the model pipeline.
paper_title: Empowering Power Outage Prediction with Spatially Aware Hybrid Graph Neural Networks and Contrastive Learning
paper_authors: Xuyang Shen, Zijie Pan, Diego Cerrai, Xinxuan Zhang, Christopher Colorio
